As a differential diagnosis, progressive encephalomyelitis with rigidity PER may be considered. However, in this case, higher-cortical functions were maintained, the cerebrospinal fluid was normal, and the brainstem symptoms were temporary while typical PER is progressive. Neuromyotonia was also ruled out because the symptoms were not localized in more distal areas and diazepam should not be as effective as in this case.
